patch_description: Instead of SLSQP on a log-sum-exp softmin with hard simplex constraints (which frequently fails/stalls and produced score 0.00 here), this approach uses a fundamentally different optimizer: projected gradient ascent directly on a softmax-weighted area objective with a barrier-free parameterization. Each iteration computes all 165 triangle areas, forms softmax weights at low temperature (heavily emphasizing the bottleneck triangles), and takes a gradient step that explicitly pushes bottleneck points apart along the direction that increases their areas. Feasibility is maintained by barycentric clipping (u,v ≥ 0, u+v ≤ 1) after every step, a cheap exact projection onto the simplex per point. Multiple deterministic restarts, an annealed step size, and a final local "pair perturbation" refinement give robustness: if optimization fails, a graceful deterministic fallback grid is returned. The bottleneck-focused gradient is far more effective at escaping the plateau than generic constrained SQP, and the whole pipeline is pure NumPy, fast and deterministic.
